findings.summary: bounded-path marker cannot fail on a stamp-encoding defect
findings.text: this assertion is meant to show the bounded path was taken, but the store-backed arm returns _current() without reading the signature at reckon/crew/open_run_index.py:737-739, and the fixture home built at :163 always has a run store, so the assertion holds whatever the signature encodes and cannot redden on a stamp-encoding regression.

the document-backed stamp comparison is exercised by no test: tests/test_the_held_worktree_screen_reads_only_open_runs.py:163 writes a run store into RECKON_HOME, so matches_sources takes the store branch at :737 and restoring the base's exact-equality comparison here reddens no assertion, leaving the branch the commit message describes as the first defect unguarded.

findings.summary: second stamp encoder beside the owned canonical one
findings.text: _stamp_text is a second "stable string for a stamp" encoder beside the owned reckon/capabilities.py:1355 pick_input_stamp_key, and unlike it the new one is dict-insertion-order dependent for the Any it accepts, so two spellings of one identity are still possible for a mapping stamp — the drift its own docstring claims to prevent.
